key_insight: Latent Memory Palace (LMP) turns control policy reasoning into autoregressive latent-space variational inference, enabling adaptive multi-step deliberation for continuous actions.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical path to more sample-efficient, interpretable control policies and better action tokenization for downstream autoregressive robotics and decision systems.
method: Model reasoning as an autoregressive latent distribution rather than in language space.
Optimize a variational lower bound with a latent-space reinforcement learning procedure.
Use the same framework to build a variable-length action tokenizer and a policy, LMP-π.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports strong empirical performance in both simulation and real-world domains, along with interpretable adaptive allocation of test-time compute.
watch_item: Training relies on variational inference and latent RL, so stability, optimization complexity, and compute overhead may be important implementation concerns.
paper_title: Latent Memory Palace: Reasoning for Control as Autoregressive Variational Inference
